decision_subject: Joint Genotyping interval strategy at 51 samples
allocation_regime: common_ceiling_comparison; every experiment shares one identical resource policy, so allocation is never the reason a compared pair differs

gates_are_separate.data_contract_gate: does the change alter scientific semantics
gates_are_separate.architecture_gate: does the change earn its resource and operational cost
gates_are_separate.note: clearing the data-contract gate makes a change eligible for comparison, never adopted by itself

E2a.change: chromosome-scale contigs split into 20 Mb windows; small scaffolds remain individual tasks
E2a.rationale: A 57.7% reduction in the GenotypeGVCFs peak, the only process that was ever near a ceiling, at no measurable wall-time cost and no workspace-size cost. It converts the memory requirement from a property of the longest contig into a property of a chosen window length, which is the lever that makes a larger cohort tractable at all. The cost is 47% more workspace files and 17 more tasks, which is scheduling overhead rather than a resource constraint. The data contract is unchanged with nothing unresolved.
E2a.cost_accepted: workspace file count rises 47.2% (3,132 to 4,611); task count rises from 36 to 53

E2b.change: bounded grouping of consecutive small scaffolds, on top of E2a's window splitting

data_contract_gate.note: every difference falls inside the comparison helper's own conservative >= 35.01 branch, so no reconstruction-limit reasoning is needed at all. Independently re-classified by the same gate applied to E2a, reaching the same result.
data_contract_gate.observed_margin_scope: this 51-sample E2a/E2b comparison only, across its 975 differing records; not a general claim that a jittered QD is always safe from the QD<2 boundary

architecture_gate.decisive_observation: The grouped task becomes the run-wide import memory maximum at 6.57 GiB, exceeding every 20 Mb chromosome window's 1.76 GiB, while covering 818,535 bp in total: less than one twenty-fourth of a single window. GenomicsDBImport's memory tracks the number of distinct contig arrays written concurrently rather than total base pairs, so grouping 25 tiny scaffolds costs 3.7 times the memory of importing 20 Mb of one chromosome.

E2b.rationale: The benefit that motivates small-scaffold grouping did not materialise. Workspace files fell 2.1% (96 of 4,611) and import wall time fell 26.9 seconds out of roughly 19,000, while run-wide import peak RSS rose 272% and the grouped task became the binding import constraint. GATK additionally fell back to serial reader initialisation for that task, discarding the eight reader threads requested. Paying a 3.7x import memory increase and losing reader parallelism, plus the standing complexity of grouping logic and its ordering constraints, to remove 96 files is not a trade worth making.
E2b.not_the_reason: This is not rejected for any scientific or data-contract problem; its callset is clean and fully explained.
E2b.revisit_if: a future reference has enough small scaffolds that per-scaffold task or file proliferation becomes a real operational constraint, or if GenomicsDBImport's per-array memory behaviour changes in a later GATK version

resulting_strategy.adopted: 20 Mb chromosome window splitting with small scaffolds as individual tasks (E2a)
resulting_strategy.note: E2b's baseline is E2a, so rejecting grouping leaves window splitting standing on its own measurements

scope_and_limits.explicitly_not_claimed: No measurement here establishes how either strategy behaves at 327 samples. The 20 Mb window peak of 7.43 GiB and the grouped-task peak of 6.57 GiB are both 51-sample figures under this reference.
scope_and_limits.window_size: 20 Mb was fixed before measurement by the protocol and was not searched over after seeing results; no claim is made that it is optimal
scope_and_limits.truth_set: none available; no accuracy claim is made for any strategy
